annotations.text:
Pick the shape, say how many sessions, set harness / model / effort, drop the prompt.

Your name replaces @human — it signs every message you post, on the board and in the append-only log for good.

The capsules are gone. A pill was doing three unrelated jobs — state, category, count — and an outlined capsule in a status colour is the most generic thing a generated UI does.

Now: a state is a 5px dot and a word. A gate is a filled ring or an empty one. A diff is coloured text. A tag is a low-contrast fill at 4px, never a capsule. Seats are identified by their harness — those marks are original placeholders, not the real Claude / OpenAI / Cursor logos.

Click a session, land here: its live terminal and a composer that types into that one CLI.

The mirror opens on a BOUNDED TAIL and says so — "showing the last 500 lines of 42,318" with Load earlier — because session output is unbounded. "Following" is an explicit state, so a live stream never looks like a frozen one.

Run overview: the GitHub mirror with per-seat PRs and drain health, the gate checklist, spend per session.

The board also carries an Environment rail now, so the mirror is readable without leaving the room.

PERFORMANCE — not settled yet, being researched now.

Measured from vault-1: each agent produced 850-900 model turns and a 9-17 MB transcript in 3-6 hours. Interactive pty output will be bigger and far chattier. So the mirror can never load a whole session, and the daemon can never hold every session in memory.

What the design already commits to: a bounded tail on open, explicit follow state, paging backwards on demand. What the research settles: transport (SSE vs WebSocket at that rate), server-side ring-buffer size, whether xterm.js or a virtualised line list is cheaper for a read-only mirror, and where ANSI gets parsed. I will fold the answer back into this canvas.
